expert_term.en: expert witness (term used in the Supreme Court Practice Directions 2021, para. 56(8)-(9)); the statutory definition in Evidence Act 1893 s. 47 was not verified

appointment.summary_en: Expert evidence requires court approval. An expert has specialised knowledge from training, study or experience.

questions.summary_en: Parties propose agreed issues and facts for court approval; the court resolves disagreement. Evidence stays within those issues and facts unless the court orders otherwise.

items_en: Signed expert report exhibited to the expert's affidavit
Qualifications and acknowledgment of the overriding duty to the court
Referred issues and agreed or assumed facts
Names, qualifications and supervision of those conducting tests or data work
Range of opinion and reasons for the chosen opinion
Belief in the correctness of the opinion

rights_duties.basis: Rules of Court 2021, Order 12 rules 1 and 6
rights_duties.summary_en: The duty to assist the court overrides duties to the instructing or paying party. The court may order expert discussions and written clarification.

procedures.scope: Civil proceedings governed by Rules of Court 2021, Order 12; criminal proceedings and any transitional or specialist-court rules require separate review.

declaration.basis: Rules of Court 2021, Order 12 rule 5(2)(b), (g); composed acknowledgment, not a prescribed oath
declaration.text_local: I understand that my duty to assist the Court within my expertise on the referred issues overrides my obligations to the person instructing or paying me. I believe my opinion is correct.
declaration.text_en: I understand that my duty to assist the Court within my expertise on the referred issues overrides my obligations to the person instructing or paying me. I believe my opinion is correct.

esignature.law_en: Electronic Transactions Act 2010: electronic signatures and secure electronic signatures; statutory exclusions and filing rules remain relevant
esignature.qualified_term_local: secure electronic signature (Singapore statutory term; not EU qualified-signature status)

timestamp.qualified_recognition: Section 19 provides rebuttable presumptions for secure records and secure signatures. It does not itself establish qualified status for a third-party RFC 3161 token. Non-secure signatures receive no authenticity or integrity presumption under this Part.

open_questions: Evidence Act 1893 s. 47 (opinions of experts) wording and scope were not verified.
Evidence Act 1893 s. 116A (presumptions in relation to electronic records) and the other computer-output / electronic-record provisions were not verified.
Criminal Procedure Code 2010 s. 263 and s. 269 (expert reports in criminal proceedings, conditions for admission without calling the expert) were not verified.
Penal Code 1871 ss. 191-193 (giving and fabricating false evidence) and current maximum penalties were not verified.
State Courts Practice Directions 2021 provisions on experts were not checked.
Singapore national adoptions of ISO/IEC 27037/27041/27042/27043 (SS ISO/IEC ...) and any official digital-forensics guidance (e.g., from the Singapore Police Force or CSA) were not verified.
Whether Singapore has a statute regulating forensic expert activity was not verified.
The applicable commencement/transitional rules, specialist-court rules, electronic filing requirements and any separate timestamp-provider regime remain to be checked for the intended proceeding.
